data.title: Blender releases their Oscar winning version tool
data.author: babuloseo
data.article_summary: Blender 4.4 聚焦于稳定性和质量提升，在“质量冬季”活动中解决了超过700个问题，并改进了技术债务和文档。新功能包括**Action Slots**，允许不同数据块共享一个动作，简化了动画工作流程。其他改进有：约束无目标时不显示关系线，图形编辑器新增F-Curve噪波修改器，骨架对称时自动镜像骨集合，以及Python API的概念性更改。视频编辑器（VSE）支持H.265编码、10/12位视频，提升了文本编辑和性能。新增H.265/HEVC编码渲染，支持10/12位色彩深度，改善了颜色转换精度。Blender扩展平台提供超过500个免费插件和主题，支持自定义和共享。建模工具新增按极点选择功能，优化了拓扑操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Blender软件的普及、发展及其相关工具与社区贡献

  - Emireladero认为Blender让3D工作变得更加“主流”，吸引了大量普通用户，且在非高端3D工作中已成为默认选择，甚至可以与Coca-Cola这样的品牌影响力相比。

  - Hermitcrab对v4.4展示视频中出现的O'Neal圆筒渲染感兴趣，询问其出处，显示用户对特定内容的关注。

• **技术支持与平台问题**：
  - Jrickert提到使用Blender 20年的经历，但担忧Hackintosh上的AMD GPU加速支持被取消后对macOS用户的影响。

- 文章标题中的“版本工具”和“奥斯卡”相关表述引发困惑，用户质疑其准确性或实际意义。

Blender 4.4 introduces

WHAT ARE

?
Before Action Slots, each data-block specific animation—like an object’s position, a camera’s depth of field, or a material’s shader properties—needed its own separate Action. This made it difficult to animate multiple elements together or share animations between objects or even projects.
For example, if you wanted to animate a camera moving while also changing its depth of field, you’d need two separate Actions, which couldn’t be easily linked or reused.
Now you can mix all sorts of animations such as an object’s position, its material properties, even compositing effects—all within a single Action.

data.title: Source code art in the Rivulet language
data.author: cranbor
data.article_summary: Rivulet是一种基于流动股线的编程语言，使用半图形字符编写。它有四种股线，每种有其独特的符号和语法规则，共同组成紧密的代码块（glyph）。Rivulet避免传统的条件分支和循环，所有股线都会执行，通过条件回滚实现分支控制。数据以包含零的相邻单元列表形式组织，命令可应用于单个单元或整个列表，并支持列表间操作。控制流按股线从左上角开始逐列执行，问题股线用于检测回滚条件。Rivulet语法复杂但易于读写，代码块通过特定标记定义和排列，股线按其起始位置顺序执行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一种新编程语言（esolang）的设计及其视觉与语法特征引发的讨论

不同观点：
• [创建者视角] rottytooth介绍了该语言的背景，说明其设计目的是将自然语言元素融入代码，避免过度逻辑化的语法，强调紧凑性和表达力。他还提到该语言将包含在一本由MIT Press出版的书中。
• [学习难度] QuadmasterXLII和vorbits表示该语言的规范非常陌生和难以理解，尤其是对于有编程经验的人来说，缺乏直观的起点。
• [视觉联想] gabetax将该语言的视觉特征与toki pona语言的sitelen musi书写系统联系起来。
• [幽默/批评] layer8和mrbluecoat以幽默的方式评论该语言可能会导致“意大利面条代码”（spaghetti code），并将其与古代文化（如玛雅）联系起来。

补充讨论：
• [对实验的欣赏] memhole和aredox表示欣赏这种实验性语言，认为在当前AI推动少数语言普及的趋势下，这种实验尤为重要。
• [艺术性] ge96和aa-jv从艺术角度赞赏该语言的美学价值，甚至设想其在公共空间中的应用。
• [工具与创意] nashashmi和nathan_douglas提出将该语言与MS Paint作为IDE或用theremin作为输入设备的创意结合，强调其跨界潜力。
• [具体实现] marmalar对该语言的quine（自产生程序）表示兴趣，提出了具体的实现问题。

争议焦点：
• 该语言的实用性与理解难度之间的矛盾，部分评论者认为其过于复杂和陌生，难以建立编写直觉。

Rivulet
Rivulet is a programming language of flowing strands, written in semigraphic characters. A strand is not pictographic: its flow does not simulate computation. There are four kinds of strands, each with their own symbolism and grammatical rules. Together, they form glyphs, tightly-packed blocks of code whose strands execute together.

Status: Version 0.4
. This is a mostly-working interpreter, and a tool to generate svg files of source code. The command list will likely need to expand for usability.
Design Philosophy
Rivulet is a list-based language that avoids ordinary approaches to branching and looping. Strands never split and no strand is left un-executed.
Its writing system was inspired by the satisfying compactness of mazes, Anni Albers's Meanders series, and space-filling algorithms. Its calligraphic aspects draw from natural language and favor the ability to write by hand.
Data Model
In Rivulet, data is organized into lists of adjacent cells, populated with zeros by default. Commands are applied to either a single cell or an entire list. They take a second parameter, a constant or the value of another cell.
Commands can also be run list-to-list, applying the command to each successive cell of one list, from the corresponding cells of the other. While these consider zero-populated cells as well, a list-to-list command ends at the last cell holding a value in either list.
The first list, List 1, is sometimes used as the output stream. This is an interpreter setting, as is whether they are displayed as numerical data or a Unicode string (where each value is rounded to the nearest integer).
Control Flow
Every strand of every glyph runs in a Rivulet program; there is no equivalent of an "if" statement. If a glyph leads to an unwanted state, that glyph and the others of its block (all contiguous glyphs of the same level or higher), can be rolled back, setting the execution state to what it was before the glyph (or set of glyphs) fired. The conditional rollback is the only form of branching in Rivulet. Loops only end with a rollback of their last iteration. Tests for rollback are that a single cell or an entire list is either zero or non-zero, indicated by a special strand called the Question Strand.
Data strands are run in the order they begin at the top left, moving through each column flowing to the right. So the strand beginning at coordinate 2,0 is run, then 2,1, then 3,0, and so on. Question strands are always run after the data strands are executed.
Syntax
Rivulet's nuanced grammar may seem overwhelming at first but becomes easy to read and write with practice.
Glyphs
Glyphs begin with markers: ╵ in the upper left and end with ╷ at the bottom right. They must not have a vertically-oriented character directly above or below them, or they'll be confused for strands. Any text outside of glyph markers is ignored.
The level of the glyph is marked by how many ╵s appear at the beginning of the glyph. Levels tell where glyphs fall within larger blocks of code.
Glyphs can be arranged vertically or side-by-side. They are read in the order of their starting marker location: top-to-bottom, left-to-right.

43492652.article_summary: Rivulet是一种基于流动股线的编程语言，使用半图形字符编写。它有四种股线，每种有其独特的符号和语法规则，共同组成紧密的代码块（glyph）。Rivulet避免传统的条件分支和循环，所有股线都会执行，通过条件回滚实现分支控制。数据以包含零的相邻单元列表形式组织，命令可应用于单个单元或整个列表，并支持列表间操作。控制流按股线从左上角开始逐列执行，问题股线用于检测回滚条件。Rivulet语法复杂但易于读写，代码块通过特定标记定义和排列，股线按其起始位置顺序执行。

data.title: I genuinely don't understand why some people are still bullish about LLMs
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 文章提到在x.com网站上，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展可能会引发问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户注意这一潜在问题，并提供了简单的解决办法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）技术的潜力和局限性，以及用户对其的不同看法和使用体验。

不同观点：
• gilbetron等用户认为LLM技术非常惊艳，尽管有局限性，但其进步速度和当前能力已经令人惊叹。他们批评一些人不切实际地期望LLM成为完美的超级智能。
• MostlyStable和josephwegner指出，使用LLM需要技能，特别是良好的提示技巧。他们强调LLM在某些简单任务上非常有效，但并不是所有情况下都是合适的工具。
• ksec和simonw关注LLM的局限性和潜在问题，特别是虚假信息和不可靠的引用，担心这会影响年轻一代的教育和知识构建。
• retrac和ttul认为当前对LLM的批评往往忽视了技术的革命性进步，并将早期问题视为技术发展中的正常现象，类似于早期数字摄影和计算机图形学的发展历程。
• crazygringo和Nevermark强调LLM的不完美是可以接受的，只要它们能够提高生产力和节省时间，特别是在学术研究和日常工作中的应用。
• iambateman指出LLM领域存在泡沫，但同时承认该技术在实际应用中产生了巨大价值，特别是在降低成本和提高效率方面。
• maple3142将LLM比喻为概率性工具，强调需要不同的使用方法来应对其不完美性。
• bjornsing分享了使用Claude进行复杂问题分析的正面体验，认为LLM对好奇和好问的人非常有价值。
• Cloudef和jandrewrogers则对LLM在内容生成和编程领域的负面影响表示担忧，认为模型在重要或复杂问题上的表现较差，且生成的内容可能误导他人。

补充讨论：
• LLM在教育中的潜在影响，特别是对年轻一代知识构建和问题解决能力的可能影响。
• LLM生成内容的真实性和伦理问题，包括模型训练数据的来源和使用是否合乎道德。
• LLM技术在不同应用场景下的适用性和局限性，以及如何根据具体需求评估其价值。
• 对LLM技术未来发展的期望和预测，包括其在多模态应用（如图像、视频生成）中的潜力。

争议的焦点：
• LLM是否能够成为可靠且高效的生产力工具，特别是在复杂和高价值任务中的应用效果。
• 用户对LLM的期望是否过高，以及如何平衡技术进步带来的热情和现实中的局限性。

data.title: Trapping misbehaving bots in an AI Labyrinth
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: Cloudflare推出了一项名为AI Labyrinth的新策略，用于应对不遵守“禁止爬取”指令的AI爬虫和其他恶意机器人。当检测到异常机器人活动时，系统会自动部署一系列由AI生成的链接页面，诱导爬虫进入，浪费其计算资源和时间，从而减缓其数据抓取效率。这些生成的内容经过预处理，确保不含安全漏洞，并且对搜索引擎和正常用户不可见。同时，AI Labyrinth还充当代蜜罐，帮助识别和标记恶意机器人，提升Cloudflare的检测能力，避免陷入与攻击者的无尽对抗中。这种方法通过使用AI生成内容进行防御，既保护了网站数据，又不影响用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare隐藏链接对不同群体的影响及其实施的公平性

不同观点：
• karaterobot认为隐藏链接可能会对使用屏幕阅读器的用户造成困扰，尽管他们自己不会受到太大影响，但对使用辅助技术的人可能有未知影响。
• __MatrixMan__引用了小说中的概念，认为隐藏误导性信息可能是为了对抗未经授权的爬虫，并将此与Cloudflare的措施联系起来。
• darth_avocado提出一种替代方案，建议通过让机器人观看广告来验证其身份，而不是使用技术手段阻挡。
• darthalthus对"没有人会深入点击四层AI生成的内容"的说法表示怀疑，暗示可能存在例外情况。
• visarga将Cloudflare的措施比作焚屋防贼，认为这种做法可能导致信息互不信任的极端情况，并联想到图像处理领域类似的破坏模型训练的方法。
• d4rkn0d3z对Cloudflare检测未经授权爬虫的技术手段表示好奇。
• LeoPanthera建议在训练大型语言模型时避免使用AI生成后的数据，认为2022年11月是LLM发展的关键时间点。
• KennyBlanken认为Cloudflare的措施更多是为了保护大公司利益，而非单纯阻止不良机器人，并指出这种做法可能抑制创新和小型竞争者。
• momojo质疑这种“军备竞赛”是否能真正阻止爬虫行为，并邀请有相关经验的人分享看法。
• gloosx对"没有人会深入点击四层AI生成的内容"的说法感到不满，认为这种判断可能误伤真实用户。
• ccgreg开玩笑地提出利用这些隐藏链接进行牟利的步骤，暗示可能存在滥用风险。
• mipsum544664认为当前措施不够具有对抗性，建议使用更具迷惑性的内容来干扰爬虫。
• zzo38computer关注禁用CSS的情况下如何处理这些隐藏链接，表明技术实施细节的重要性。
• ceroxylon指出Cloudflare引用的Medium上AI生成内容比例数据存在争议，强调了信息准确性的问题。
• seasluggy对"没有人会深入点击四层AI生成的内容"的说法表示怀疑，认为可能存在例外情况。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术手段公平性和对小网站、小型创新者的影响成为一个争议焦点。
• 用户对Cloudflare和其他大公司合作以抑制竞争的担忧也在讨论中被提及。
• 技术实施细节（如CSS禁用情况下的链接处理）和信息准确性（如Medium数据争议）也是值得注意的讨论点。

43411725.article_content:
Trapping misbehaving bots in an AI Labyrinth
2025-03-19
Reid Tatoris
Harsh Saxena
Luis Miglietti
5 min read
Today, weâre excited to announce AI Labyrinth, a new mitigation approach that uses AI-generated content to slow down, confuse, and waste the resources of AI Crawlers and other bots that donât respect âno crawlâ directives. When you opt in, Cloudflare will automatically deploy an AI-generated set of linked pages when we detect inappropriate bot activity, without the need for customers to create any custom rules.
AI Labyrinth is available on an opt-in basis to all customers, including the
Free plan
.
Using Generative AI as a defensive weapon
AI-generated content has exploded, reportedly accounting for
four of the top 20 Facebook posts
last fall. Additionally, Medium estimates that
47% of all content
on their platform is AI-generated. Like any newer tool it has both wonderful and
malicious
uses.
At the same time, weâve also seen an explosion of new crawlers used by AI companies to scrape data for model training. AI Crawlers generate more than 50 billion requests to the Cloudflare network every day, or just under 1% of all web requests we see. While Cloudflare has several tools for
identifying and blocking unauthorized AI crawling
, we have found that blocking malicious
bots
can alert the attacker that you are on to them, leading to a shift in approach, and a never-ending arms race. So, we wanted to create a new way to thwart these unwanted bots, without letting them know theyâve been thwarted.
To do this, we decided to use a new offensive tool in the bot creatorâs toolset that we havenât really seen used defensively: AI-generated content. When we detect unauthorized crawling, rather than blocking the request, we will link to a series of AI-generated pages that are convincing enough to entice a crawler to traverse them. But while real looking, this content is not actually the content of the site we are protecting, so the crawler wastes time and resources.Â
As an added benefit, AI Labyrinth also acts as a next-generation honeypot. No real human would go four links deep into a maze of AI-generated nonsense. Any visitor that does is very likely to be a bot, so this gives us a brand-new tool to identify and fingerprint bad bots, which we add to our list of known bad actors. Hereâs how we do itâ¦
How we built the labyrinthÂ
When AI crawlers follow these links, they waste valuable computational resources processing irrelevant content rather than extracting your legitimate website data. This significantly reduces their ability to gather enough useful information to train their models effectively.
To generate convincing human-like content, we used
Workers AI
with an open source model to create unique HTML pages on diverse topics. Rather than creating this content on-demand (which could impact performance), we implemented a pre-generation pipeline that sanitizes the content to
prevent any XSS vulnerabilities
, and stores it in
R2
for faster retrieval. We found that generating a diverse set of topics first, then creating content for each topic, produced more varied and convincing results. It is important to us that we donât generate inaccurate content that contributes to the spread of misinformation on the Internet, so the content we generate is real and related to scientific facts, just not relevant or proprietary to the site being crawled.
This pre-generated content is seamlessly integrated as hidden links on existing pages via our custom HTML transformation process, without disrupting the original structure or content of the page. Each generated page includes appropriate meta directives to protect SEO by preventing search engine indexing. We also ensured that these links remain invisible to human visitors through carefully implemented attributes and styling. To further minimize the impact to regular visitors, we ensured that these links are presented only to suspected AI scrapers, while allowing legitimate users and verified crawlers to browse normally.
A graph of daily requests over time, comparing different categories of AI Crawlers.
What makes this approach particularly effective is its role in our continuously evolving bot detection system. When these links are followed, we know with high confidence that it's automated crawler activity, as human visitors and legitimate browsers would never see or click them. This provides us with a powerful identification mechanism, generating valuable data that feeds into our
machine learning models
. By analyzing which crawlers are following these hidden pathways, we can identify new bot patterns and signatures that might otherwise go undetected. This proactive approach helps us stay ahead of AI scrapers, continuously improving our detection capabilities without disrupting the normal browsing experience.

data.title: Abundance isn't going to happen unless politicians are scared of the status quo
data.author: viajante1882
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了实现“丰裕”（Abundance）目标的挑战，强调政治家需要对现状感到压力，才能推动变革。作者以加州住房问题为例，指出尽管有许多善意的法律，但它们反而阻碍了新住房的建设。当前，“丰裕”理念强调以结果为导向，关注实际成果而非过程，呼吁增加住房、移民和清洁能源等。然而，政府在实现这些目标时面临能力不足的问题，部分原因是程序繁琐和政治障碍。文章指出，政府应更注重实际成果，而非繁复的程序和反对机制，以提高国家能力并实现丰裕社会。这一理念虽显而易见，但在实践中却难以落实。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YIMBY主义与住房政策的可行性、政治与社会因素对住房政策的影响、政府角色与公共政策的有效性

不同观点：
• **legitster**：对YIMBY主义的成效持怀疑态度。尽管通过了新的分区法律允许建造附属住宅单元（ADUs），但由于房主对成为房东的恐惧以及他们经济状况较好，缺乏动力去实际建造。因此，仅仅去除繁文缛节可能不够，还需要激励个体去行动。

• **dkjaudyeqooe**：认为自由派政治家应优先考虑住房和基础设施，而不是纠缠于社会问题。通过改善人民生活和对抗既得利益者，可以获得广泛的政治支持。

• **avidiax**：认为政客更关注现有选区成员的利益，而不是潜在的新成员。更多的可负担住房可能会降低房地产价值，因此会遭到现有房主的强烈反对。

• **norir**：认为YIMBY运动没有解决更深层次的社会问题，如身份认同和疏离感。单纯依靠政策无法解决这些情感问题，需要一个能够解决这些精神层面问题的反运动。

• **thegrim33**：对文章的论述感到困惑，认为其逻辑混乱，无法理解作者对大政府角色的立场。

• **huijzer**：提到Noah Smith对《Abundance》一书的评论，强调关注输出而不是输入，认为这样可以更有效地解决问题。

• **nimish**：指出老年人“就地养老”现象，影响了新一代的发展机会。

• **Bhilai**：支持丰裕议程，反对共和党撕裂一切的哲学，认为政府在州一级扩权的同时声称政府无效是虚伪的。

• **veltas**：强调需要更多有技能和年轻的移民，而不是简单地讨论是否接受移民，政策需要更细致。

• **JansjoFromIkea**：认为Build Back Better计划与丰裕议程有相似目标，但感觉这些计划缺乏可实现性。

• **lenerdenator**：认为由于经济资源雄厚的政治人物的阻挠，改革将需要很长时间。

• **nielsbot**：引用Paul Glastris的观点，认为YIMBY主义激怒了当地居民，而重新分区商业区能建造更多住房单元。

• **keepamovin**：提出“适度贫困理论”，认为政府可能有意维持一定程度的匮乏以保持自身稳定。

• **TulliusCicero**：讨论CEQA法律的环境保护初衷与被滥用于阻止发展项目的现实，指出过程导向可能导致不良结果。

• **HaZeust**：认为不仅仅是吓唬政客，现有房主也常常阻止改变，建议需要结构性杠杆，赋予公民和企业直接施压的能力。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：YIMBY主义是否足够有效，去除繁文缛节与激励措施的平衡，政客与房主对政策变化的态度。
• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：移民政策的具体化，政府在住房政策中的角色与影响，社会疏离感与政治运动的关系。

这些观点反映了住房政策的多维度挑战，包括政治、社会和经济因素的复杂互动。

“
Too many goods created a bad
.”
That’s how California Governor Jerry Brown put it in 2017 when he signed a package of 15 housing-related bills, the first YIMBY-supported pro-housing bills. He was explaining, in his meandering way, how the housing shortage was the result of hundreds of well-intentioned laws, which had promised all kinds of things, but mostly succeeded in slowing down the production of new housing.
In many ways, Jerry was ahead of the curve. He was lamenting “
everything bagel liberalism
” and “
process over outcomes”
before it was cool.
But at the same time, there was a distinct lack of fire under the Governor’s ass. He was skeptical that this new legislation would do much to unwind the tangled legal web holding back housing production. And while we YIMBYs were bright eyed and bushy tailed, seeing as it was the first state bill signing we’d been invited to, it was also kind of depressing.
Less than ten years later, the discourse is suddenly
all about
the seemingly simple idea that we should “do things and build things,” and there is finally a sense of urgency. I’m heading to Atlanta this week to interview Derek Thompson about his new book
Abundance
with Ezra Klein at the Georgia Center for the Book (
tickets
). Their thesis is simple: we need more of everything. More housing, more immigrants, more clean energy infrastructure.
And Klein and Thomson’s book is just the latest entry into the growing genre that attempts to address the root causes of stagnation in America and prescribe a path towards abundance and renewal. Recent books in this genre include:
Why Nothing Works
by Marc J. Dunkelman
Stuck
by Yoni Applebaum,
Recoding America
by Jennifer Pahlka,
Meanwhile Ned Resnikoff is
pointing out that YIMBYs were doing abundance before it was cool (or maybe were the driving force in making it cool)
. While I appreciate the credit to the original YIMBY brand, I’m choosing to adopt an abundance mindset about abundance. More is more, after all.
Subscribe
As I see it, the Abundance concept isn’t quite an ideology, it’s more of a refocusing on outcomes. It’s a framework that points to tangible outcomes and asks us to tactically identify what is blocking progress to that goal, irrespective of what the intention of that blockage might be. It extends the classic YIMBY way of doing politics into a larger philosophy. It is a re-focusing on “ends” over “means,” and allows for a variety of ideologies to come together on specific ends. The language around “outcomes focused legislating” brings some degree of sanity to our often self-sabotaging process.
Outcome-based politics seems so obvious that it can sound silly to say it out loud. Government should deliver material outcomes. Elected officials should be extremely motivated to produce tangible outcomes for the largest number of people.
So why isn’t that happening?
What’s eating state capacity?
The hot topic in the growing abundance discourse is
state capacity
. That’s a fancy term for a simple concept — the government’s ability to deliver outcomes, whether those are growing the economy, establishing laws, or just picking up the garbage.
It’s not a new idea. In fact, five decades ago, some of the world’s most pre-eminent political scientists fretted about the erosion of state capacity in democracies across the world. “The demands on democratic government grow,”
wrote Michael Crozier, Samuel Huntington, and Joji Watanuki
, “while the capacity of democratic government stagnates.”
Sounds familiar, doesn’t it? They argued that in countries like the United States, Japan, and Western Europe, citizens were asking their governments to take on more and more without increasing their government’s ability to carry out those projects. That led to an erosion in legitimacy, and decades of retrenchment and cutbacks. About the only thing that the left and the right seemed to agree on was that the “
era of big government is over
.”
The 70’s was an era of community organizing to stop The Big Bad Thing, and this urge to tap the brakes continues to this day. Elaborate outreach processes, reporting requirements and the opportunities for objections about those reports… they all can seem reasonable. But added together they created a mighty web. Marc Dunkelman explained the problem of this approach on
a recent episode of the Political Gabfest
: “We've now created a system where there are so many veto players and you need so many approvals that government fundamentally doesn't work.”

data.title: Show HN: Multi UPS SNMP based shutdown
data.author: PhilKunz
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用基于Node.js的自动更新UPS工具与传统的Network UPS Tools（NUT）的对比及可行性讨论

不同观点：
• [反对观点 - windsurfer]  
  - 认为没有必要使用基于Node.js的自动更新UPS工具，因为传统的Network UPS Tools已经经过长时间验证，并且大多数Linux发行版已经预装。  
  - 质疑为何要选择可能不稳定的新技术，而不是使用成熟、稳定的解决方案。

• [支持但有保留的观点 - exabrial]  
  - 对项目发起人的主动性表示赞赏，但认为Node.js不适合用于关键任务如UPS管理。  
  - 具体指出Node.js存在较多bug，且API的生命周期较短（只有几周），不适合长期稳定运行的系统。  
  - 对自动更新持反对态度，认为UPS守护进程连接到互联网是不必要的，可能带来安全和其他问题。  
  - 尽管对技术实现有保留意见，但对项目的文档表示赞赏，认为其清晰美观。  
  - 对比NUT的配置，认为虽然NUT配置不难，但也不够优秀，存在改进空间。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点主要在于是否应该采用基于Node.js的自动更新UPS工具，反对者认为传统工具已经足够好，支持者则认为新工具在某些方面（如文档）有优势，但在技术选择（Node.js）和自动更新方面存在隐患。
• 对Node.js的稳定性和适用性存在较大分歧，支持者承认其在某些方面有改进空间，但对其API不稳定和守护进程连接互联网持强烈保留态度。

data.title: Conquest of the Incas
data.author: remarkEon
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了西班牙征服者如何以极小的军事力量征服庞大的美洲原住民帝国，重点介绍了弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗征服印加帝国的过程。文章比较了埃尔南·科尔特斯征服阿兹特克帝国和皮萨罗征服印加帝国的案例，两者都以少量的西班牙士兵（分别约400和180人）成功征服了数百万人口的帝国。作者分析了西班牙人成功的因素，包括卓越的领导能力、技术优势以及外交手段。文章还详细描述了印加帝国的组织结构、扩张方式及其高效的行政管理体系，指出印加人通过间接统治、强制劳役等手段维持对广阔领土的控制。作者引用了贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯的《新西班牙的征服》一书中的第一手资料，描述了西班牙征服者在入侵过程中目睹的残酷场景。最后，作者反思了自己对这段历史的浓厚兴趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对美洲原住民历史及其与欧洲征服者互动的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• **didgetmaster** 认为，现代美国人常被教育或媒体误导，以为在欧洲人到来之前，美洲原住民部落彼此和平共处，但实际上部落间经常发生战争，野蛮行为如屠杀、奴役、强奸和人祭等也很常见。他指出，这种叙事忽视了历史的复杂性，虽然欧洲征服者也做了许多坏事，但原住民并非全然无辜。

• **mbil** 引用了Graeber的论点，认为前现代文明并不主要依赖物物交换系统，而是使用债务追踪系统，例如印加帝国的khipu系统。这表明印加帝国的运作方式可能比通常认为的更为复杂，且与欧亚大陆的债务概念有相似之处。

• **acyou** 讨论了印加人面临欧洲征服者时的可能战略，如非直接军事对抗，而是采取消耗战、限制敌方行动、使用毒箭和夜间突袭等。他认为，协调大量人口进行这些行动是主要挑战，军事力量并非唯一决定因素，软实力同样重要。

• **inglor_cz** 对比了印加帝国和波斯在被征服后的不同命运，认为印加帝国的组织能力因大量人口死亡而丧失，而波斯则在被征服后迅速恢复了影响力。他还指出，印加的劳役税收制度可能在防止腐败方面有其优势。

43478789.article_content:
I wrote about the
Spanish conquest of the Aztecs
five years ago during the early days of this blog. The conquistadors have since remained a fascination of mine, but I haven’t had a chance to go back to them until recently when I read Bernal Diaz’s
The Conquest of New Spain
and then
The Last Days of the Incas
by Kim MacQuarrie. My goal was to get a thorough understanding of the two major Spanish New World conquests and
how
small Western military forces achieved such stunning successes over gargantuan native empires.
In the case of Hernan Cortes, about 400 Spanish soldiers (later increased to over 1,000) subjugated the Mexican Empire of about 6 million inhabitants. In the case of Francisco Pizarro, about 180 Spanish soldiers (eventually rising to over 1,000, but with rarely more than 500 ever concentrated in one place) conquered the Inca Empire of maybe 10 million inhabitants. In both cases, the Spanish invaders had almost no understanding of the local politics, geography, culture, religion, or people they were invading. In both cases, the expedition leaders deserve a ton of credit for extraordinary leadership and competence while leveraging a technological imbalance to achieve a staggering military force and diplomatic multiplier.
Since I already wrote about the Aztecs, this essay is primarily focused on Pizarro’s conquest of the Incas, which, as a reader, I found no less insane, exciting, ridiculous, and fascinating based on MacQuarrie’s fantastic
The Last Days of the Incas
. I want to present the most straightforward account of what happened and why with enough detail to get a sense of the difficulty and enormity of the conquest, but pared down enough to make the story digestible. I’ll also intersperse some of the most interesting points I learned from
The Conquest of New Spain
, which is translated from a first-hand account of one of the conquistadors present at the invasion of the Aztec Empire. At the end, I reflect a bit on why I find this stuff so interesting and can’t stop thinking about it.
https://www.pinterest.com/pin/393150242452307432/
The Incas
The Incas were/are an ethnic group based around Cusco, a city that sits at an elevation over 11,000 feet (3,300 meters) in what is today inland Peru. At the height of their power, a mere 100,000 ethnic Incas dominated an empire of 8-10 million inhabitants stretching from southern Colombia to northern Chile, from the edge of the Amazon rainforest, over the Andes, and to the Pacific coast. In the 16
th
century, Cusco’s population may have been as large as 200,000, making it comparable to Paris at the time. They called their country/nation/state/whatever you want to classify it: Tawantinsuyu.
When Francisco Pizarro first arrived at Incan land in 1528, the Incas had only expanded outside the Cusco valley for about 200 years, had only been a genuine empire for about 100 years, and had conquered most of its territory over about the last 60 years. Their expansion stopped not due to any failings on the Incas’ part, but because they had beaten every significant civilization in their vicinity, and all that was left on their borders were small villages and disorganized nomads in dense tropical jungles or sparse mountain ranges.
https://mapoftheday.quickworld.com/posts/the-inca-empire
If there was a secret sauce that gave the Inca an edge over their neighbors, it was probably
organization
. Their civilization was based in fertile valleys nestled between some of the tallest mountain peaks in the Western hemisphere. They got good at terrace farming, roads, transport, communication, infrastructure, and other logistics that permitted the formation of larger armies than their competitors.
It helped that the Incan conquest modus operandi was relatively
indirect
. The standard procedure was to bribe, threaten, or fight rival city-states into submission, then decapitate or co-opt the leadership, and then install Incan governors while keeping much of the prior state apparatus intact. The Incas preferred to harness long-term productive yields from populations in new territory rather than indulging in plunder. In lieu of taxes, every able-bodied adult male in the Incan Empire was legally required to work for the state for three months per year, or at least send their wives or children in their stead. This mass of labor, which eventually reached into the millions, produced potatoes, meat (llama or alpaca mostly), wool (same), gold, and other goods for the state, as well as building its palaces and extensive road system. Seemingly much more so than the Aztecs and comparable civilizations, the Inca understood that their power was based in its people and their production.
There is a part early in
Conquest of New Spain
when Bernal Dias describes walking into a village and finding a pile of disemboweled native bodies that had been recently ritualistically sacrificed, and then Dias says that such sights were so common in so many villages that he is going to stop describing them, but t
43478789.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了西班牙征服者如何以极小的军事力量征服庞大的美洲原住民帝国，重点介绍了弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗征服印加帝国的过程。文章比较了埃尔南·科尔特斯征服阿兹特克帝国和皮萨罗征服印加帝国的案例，两者都以少量的西班牙士兵（分别约400和180人）成功征服了数百万人口的帝国。作者分析了西班牙人成功的因素，包括卓越的领导能力、技术优势以及外交手段。文章还详细描述了印加帝国的组织结构、扩张方式及其高效的行政管理体系，指出印加人通过间接统治、强制劳役等手段维持对广阔领土的控制。作者引用了贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯的《新西班牙的征服》一书中的第一手资料，描述了西班牙征服者在入侵过程中目睹的残酷场景。最后，作者反思了自己对这段历史的浓厚兴趣。

data.title: iCloud Mail has DNS misconfigured?
data.author: wildekek
data.article_summary: 这封电子邮件来自willem@vooijs.eu，主题为“hi”，发送时间为2025年3月29日。邮件通过了SPF和DKIM认证，并且DMARC验证结果为通过。根据SpamAssassin的检测，邮件的垃圾评分是1.3，低于判定为垃圾邮件的阈值-5，因此不被视为垃圾邮件。邮件内容简单，仅包含“This is it”。技术细节显示邮件经过苹果的邮件服务器发送，并通过了病毒和垃圾邮件检查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iCloud自定义域和邮件服务的问题与用户体验

不同观点：
• wildekek认为，之前57.103.74.0/24块没有PTR记录的问题已经解决，但现在Apple发送邮件时使用了没有PTR记录的新IP，这与Apple自身接收邮件时的标准不一致。
• Avamander指出，Microsoft最近也有类似的行为，发送没有PTR记录的邮件，但他们都对接收方要求严格。
• rreichel03分享了iCloud自定义域刚推出时的缓存MX记录bug，Apple最终修复了该问题，但没有提供奖励。
• wildekek还提到，Apple在发送邮件时使用了错误的EHLO域，导致邮件无法发送，且Apple的一线支持无法解决此问题。
• Polizeioposaune引用了mailop邮件列表中的讨论，提到Apple已经意识到该问题。
• djhworld表示对iCloud自定义域失去信心，因为经常丢失个人对个人的邮件，导致其切换到fastmail。
• indigodaddy对iCloud没有A记录表示惊讶。
• MisterBiggs提到，使用iCloud自定义域一年后，最近首次遇到邮件发送失败的问题。
• zeagle描述了从migadu切换到iCloud的经历，提到iCloud在处理别名和邮件转发时存在问题，有时邮件会被退回。
• Galaco列举了iCloud自定义域和邮件的多个bug，包括无法使用曾关联过Apple账户的自定义邮箱地址，且Apple的客户支持无法有效解决问题。
• ctippett放弃了使用iCloud邮件，因为很多入站邮件被无声丢弃，且Hide My Email功能也存在可送达性问题。
• jlund-molfese表示其自定义iCloud域运行良好，没有遇到问题。
• FaridIO分享了其iCloud邮件的测试结果，显示稍有不足但整体较好。
• diegoholiveira提到，其iCloud自定义域的问题仅限于无法接收来自两个Gmail账户的邮件。

补充讨论：
• 用户对iCloud邮件服务的可靠性存在不满，尤其是邮件丢失和退信问题。
• Apple客户支持在处理技术问题时被认为无效或不足。
• 不同用户之间的体验差异显著，有些用户遇到严重问题，而有些用户则几乎没有遇到问题。
• 有用户提到Apple在处理邮件相关的技术问题时反应迟缓或不充分。

争议焦点：
• Apple在发送邮件时使用没有PTR记录的IP，与其接收邮件时的标准不一致，引发用户不满。
• iCloud自定义域和邮件服务的多个技术问题和bug，以及Apple客户支持的有效性成为争议的焦点。

• rreichel03分享了iCloud自定义域刚推出时的缓存MX记录bug，Apple最终修复了该问题，但没有提供奖励。
• wildekek还提到，Apple在发送邮件时使用了错误的EHLO域，导致邮件无法发送，且Apple的一线支持无法解决此问题。
• Polizeioposaune引用了mailop邮件列表中的讨论，提到Apple已经意识到该问题。
• djhworld表示对iCloud自定义域失去信心，因为经常丢失个人对个人的邮件，导致其切换到fastmail。
• indigodaddy对iCloud没有A记录表示惊讶。
• MisterBiggs提到，使用iCloud自定义域一年后，最近首次遇到邮件发送失败的问题。
• zeagle描述了从migadu切换到iCloud的经历，提到iCloud在处理别名和邮件转发时存在问题，有时邮件会被退回。
• Galaco列举了iCloud自定义域和邮件的多个bug，包括无法使用曾关联过Apple账户的自定义邮箱地址，且Apple的客户支持无法有效解决问题。
• ctippett放弃了使用iCloud邮件，因为很多入站邮件被无声丢弃，且Hide My Email功能也存在可送达性问题。
• jlund-molfese表示其自定义iCloud域运行良好，没有遇到问题。
• FaridIO分享了其iCloud邮件的测试结果，显示稍有不足但整体较好。
• diegoholiveira提到，其iCloud自定义域的问题仅限于无法接收来自两个Gmail账户的邮件。

补充讨论：
• 用户对iCloud邮件服务的可靠性存在不满，尤其是邮件丢失和退信问题。
• Apple客户支持在处理技术问题时被认为无效或不足。
• 不同用户之间的体验差异显著，有些用户遇到严重问题，而有些用户则几乎没有遇到问题。
• 有用户提到Apple在处理邮件相关的技术问题时反应迟缓或不充分。

争议焦点：
• Apple在发送邮件时使用没有PTR记录的IP，与其接收邮件时的标准不一致，引发用户不满。
• iCloud自定义域和邮件服务的多个技术问题和bug，以及Apple客户支持的有效性成为争议的焦点。

data.title: The Gen X Career Meltdown
data.author: littlexsparkee
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同世代对技术发展、职业变化和代际标签的看法与感受

不同观点：
• desertmonad（Gen X）认为技术曾经是探索的工具，而现在变得无处不在，令人感到怀旧。他对年轻一代表示同情，指出成长过程一直充满挑战，而现在由于在线欺凌和枪击事件等问题，挑战更为复杂。
• ohnoitsahuman（Gen X）强调Gen X通过适应和前进，表现良好，并认为那些无法调整自己行为的人才会遇到问题。
• etempleton（无明确代际标签）指出营销和新闻行业的高淘汰率和职业不稳定性，特别是年龄较大的人员在这些行业中难以维持职业生涯。
• aledalgrande（无明确代际标签）批评与代际相关的文章和讨论，认为这些讨论往往以偏概全，忽视了每个世代中都有各种类型的人。
• newfocogi（无明确代际标签）认为Gen X在拒绝父母的世界后，看到它消失并被更空虚的东西取代。
• n_ary（无明确代际标签）关注技术进步带来的低质量问题，强调人类触感在创意内容中的重要性，并批评现代商业模式中的错误激励和道德问题。
• mixmastamyk（无明确代际标签）以软件开发者的身份分享自己对职业变化的观察，指出即使是技术行业也难以避免这些变化带来的影响。
• Clubber（Gen X）认为技术整合了曾经分散的行业，使得年轻世代失去了一些职业机会，并希望全球化和技术对劳动力的冲击能有所缓解。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于代际标签和每代人所面临的职业挑战，特别是技术进步对不同行业的影响。
- 讨论中多次提到年龄歧视、职业不稳定性和行业变化对个人职业生涯的冲击。
- 有人对技术进步带来的低质量和错误激励提出批评，认为现代商业模式缺乏长远考虑。
- 部分讨论者对代际讨论本身表示反感，认为这种讨论往往缺乏深度和准确性。
- 技术对各行业的影响以及全球化对劳动力的冲击是贯穿多个观点的重要主题。

data.title: Testing Without Mocks: A Pattern Language (2023)
data.author: jcartw
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了自动化测试的重要性以及常见问题，尤其是广泛测试和使用mock（模拟）测试的弊端。广泛测试速度慢且不稳定，而mock测试虽然快且可靠，但会锁定代码实现，使重构困难，且需要补充广泛测试。文章提出了一种不使用广泛测试和mock的替代方案，即结合"可社交的状态测试"和"Nullables"技术，以避免上述问题。Nullables看似测试替身，但实际上是生产代码的一部分，具有"关闭"开关。这种方法保证了测试的速度、可靠性和可维护性，但需要在生产代码中加入Nullables，这是其主要权衡。文章还提供了具体代码示例和模式，如A-Frame架构和基础设施包装器，以帮助实现这种测试方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于测试代码时如何使用测试替身（test doubles）、模拟对象（mocks）以及其他技术的方法和原则的讨论。

不同观点：
• [bccdee] 支持文章中的方法，认为每个代码模块应该封装自己的测试替身配置和注入，通过一组测试工厂来实现。这种方法强调将测试配置的细节隐藏在模块内部，简化单元测试的编写。
• [aszen] 认为文章中没有提出新的观点，主张测试应涵盖代码的所有副作用和基础设施。建议通过使用轻量级的生产环境替代品（如SQLite、内存文件系统等）来实现快速且确定的测试。
• [sethammons] 认为文章中的概念大多是有价值的，但反对使用模拟框架，主张避免模拟，支持使用伪造对象（Fakes）和伪造构造函数。同时，提供了相关阅读材料支持其观点。
• [fhd2] 对文章中的观点感到困惑，认为文章中手工定义的模拟对象（Mock）和传统的Mock没有明显区别，质疑文章中的术语使用。
• [loevborg] 高度评价文章，认为其中的概念和模式改变了其编写软件的方式，尤其是在大型项目中的应用效果显著。但同时指出团队推广这些方法存在难度。
• [jbjbjbjb] 质疑文章中“nullables”与传统模拟对象的区别，认为只是将模拟对象的实现移到了生产代码中。
• [hyperbolablabla] 认为文章过长且术语过多，分散了核心信息的传达。
• [earnestinger] 认为文章的标题具有误导性，实际内容是手工编写测试替身和应用程序结构的建议，而非读者期望的领域特定语言（DSL）。
• [rat87] 支持使用记录/重放（record/replay）风格的测试方法，结合本地文件数据库测试，以实现快速单元测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于文章中提出的方法是否真正区别于传统的模拟对象使用，以及这些方法是否能简化测试和生产代码的维护。
• 不同观点还涉及测试的范围和深度，一方主张测试所有副作用和基础设施，另一方则关注测试代码的简化和模块化。
• 术语的使用和文章长度也被指出作为阅读和理解的障碍。

43470192.article_content:
Automated tests are important. Without them, programmers waste a huge amount of time manually checking and fixing their code.
Unfortunately, many automated tests
also
waste a huge amount of time. The easy, obvious way to write tests is to make
broad tests
that are automated versions of manual tests. But they’re flaky and slow.
Folks in the know use mocks and spies (I say “mocks” for short in this article) to write isolated
interaction-based tests
. Their tests are reliable and fast, but they tend to “lock in” implementation, making refactoring difficult, and they have to be supplemented with broad tests. It’s also easy to make poor-quality tests that are hard to read, or end up only testing themselves.
Bad tests are a sign of bad design, so some people use techniques such as
Hexagonal Architecture
and
functional core, imperative shell
to separate logic from infrastructure. (Infrastructure is code that involves external systems or state.) It fixes the problem... for logic. But infrastructure is often left untested, and it requires architectural changes that are out of reach for people with existing code.
This pattern language
1
describes a fourth option. It avoids all the above problems: it doesn’t use broad tests, doesn’t use mocks, doesn’t ignore infrastructure, and doesn’t require architectural changes. It has the speed, reliability, and maintainability of unit tests and the power of broad tests. But it’s not without
tradeoffs
of its own.
1
The structure of this article was inspired by Ward Cunningham’s
CHECKS Pattern Language of Information Integrity
, which is a model of clarity and usefulness.
The patterns combine
sociable
,
state-based
tests with a novel infrastructure technique called “
Nullables
.” At first glance, Nullables look like test doubles, but they're actually production code with an “off” switch. And that’s the tradeoff: do you want that in your production code? Your answer determines whether this pattern language is for you.
The rest of the article goes into detail. Don’t be intimidated by its size. It’s broken up into bite-sized pieces with lots of code examples.
Additional resources
For more resources related to Nullables and the “Testing Without Mocks” patterns, including screencasts, self-guided training, and more, see the
Nullables Hub
.

Conclusion
Examples
Here’s an example of testing a simple command line application. The application reads a string from the command line, encodes it using
ROT-13
, and outputs the result.
The production code uses the optional
A-Frame Architecture
pattern.
App
is the application entry point. It depends on
Rot13
, a
Logic
class, and
CommandLine
, an
Infrastructure
class. Additional patterns are mentioned in the source code.
// Example production code (JavaScript + Node.js)
import CommandLine from "./infrastructure/command_line";  //
Infrastructure Wrapper
import * as rot13 from "./logic/rot13";
export default class App {
constructor(commandLine = CommandLine.create()) {   //
Parameterless Instantiation
this._commandLine = commandLine;
}
run() {
const args = this._commandLine.args();
if (args.length === 0) {
// Tested by Test #2
this._commandLine.writeOutput("Usage: run text_to_transform\n");
return;
}
if (args.length !== 1) {
// Tested by Test #3
this._commandLine.writeOutput("too many arguments\n");
return;
}
// Tested by Test #1
const input = args[0];                          //
Logic Sandwich
const output = rot13.transform(input);
this._commandLine.writeOutput(output + "\n");
}
};
The tests of
App
look like end-to-end integration tests, but they’re actually
unit tests
. Technically, they’re
Narrow
,
Sociable
tests, which means they’re unit tests that execute code in dependencies.
As narrow tests, the tests only care about testing
App.run()
. Each of the dependencies is expected to have tests of their own, which they do.
The tests use a
Nullable
CommandLine
to throw away
stdout
and
Configurable Responses
to provide pre-configured command-line arguments. They also use
Output Tracking
to see what would have been written to
stdout
.

import CommandLine from "./infrastructure/command_line";
import App from "./app";
describe("App", () => {
// Test #1

data.title: Apple needs a Snow Sequoia
data.author: trbutler
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了苹果公司需要进行一次类似“Snow Leopard”的系统升级，以解决当前软件中的各种问题。作者回顾了2009年发布的Snow Leopard，认为它通过减少过时功能和优化系统底层，成为苹果最稳定的软件版本之一。相比之下，作者认为如今的macOS Sequoia和iOS/iPadOS 18存在诸多明显且易重现的漏洞，如Messages应用的复制粘贴问题、同步缓慢和资源占用过高等。此外，一些设计决策也被认为是倒退，如系统设置中显示排列的繁琐步骤。作者指出，这些问题影响了用户体验，呼吁苹果进行一次专注于细节和优化的“Snow”版本升级。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple软件质量下降以及更广泛的软件质量问题

不同观点：
• [rcarmo] 认为Apple的软件质量（尤其是macOS）在下降，特别是Spotlight搜索功能和软件QA的质量。他将自己视为UNIX用户，而非单纯的Mac用户，并考虑使用GNOME作为长期桌面环境。
• [hamstergene] 认为不仅是Apple，整个软件行业的产品都变得更加buggy，包括网站、应用程序和游戏等，普遍存在质量下降的问题。
• [spudlyo] 对macOS的质量下降表示不满，特别是System Settings的缓慢响应，但同时承认一些新功能如Universal Control和Continuity Camera的优点。
• [pavel_lishin] 不认为Apple落后于Windows或Android，并表示尽管Windows存在界面不一致的问题，自己仍愿意回到Apple的生态系统。

Mar 19, 2025
Apple Needs a Snow Sequoia
By
Timothy R. Butler
| Posted at
5:35 PM
The same year Apple launched the iPhone, it unveiled a massive upgrade to Mac OS X known as Leopard, sporting â300 New Features.â Two years later, it did something almost unheard of: it released Snow Leopard, an upgrade all about how
little
it added and how much it took away. Apple needs to make it snow again.
Snow Leopard did what it was made to do. It was one of the most solid software releases Apple ever put out. Iâd say one of the best modern operating system releases, period.
After Appleâs frenetic run of overhauling and quickly iterating on the entire Mac platform in the early 2000s, becoming a major technology player again with the iPod, moving the Mac to a new processor architecture (for the second of three times) and releasing the iPhone, it was time for detail work. 2009âs Snow Leopard was understated, but improved the underlying system while
shrinking
it in size by removing outdated accretions.
In an era when people still paid money for operating system upgrades every few years (anyone else remember standing in line for Windows 95?), releasing an OS upgrade without huge new features was unusual. But, it was the right idea and cemented one of the best eras of the Mac.
Nowadays, Apple includes the system upgrades in the upfront cost of its computers, so the incentive to constantly roll out ten or twenty or three hundred ânew featuresâ
should
be lower. Inexplicably, since the company adopted that no extra charge, yearly release cadence, it has seemingly been more reticent to do a disciplined âSnowâ release, no matter how necessary.
The latest releases — MacOS Sequoia and iOS/iPadOS 18 — are
screaming
for such a reset. Yes, they work and are still smoother and less glitchy than Windows 11, but they feel like software developed by people who donât actually use that software. In the 22 years since I became
a âswitcherâ
, this is the worst state I can remember Appleâs platforms being in.
Some bugs are inevitable with major releases, sure. The troubling aspect is that many are easily reproducible across devices and show up in high-traffic areas, not just forgotten nooks.
How do Appleâs engineers not notice these problems?
Take Messages. Appleâs iMessage and SMS tool is an essential app for communication for me and, I suspect, the vast majority of Apple users. Since the release of Sequoia last fall, one can no longer reliably cut or copy text from the Mac app. Attempting to copy a message bubble is a game of roulette: the message may copy or it may not.
Who knows until you try to paste!
Select text in a message and attempt to copy a specific part and it will copy… the whole message, not the selected portion. This is basic, nailed-down-in-the-1980s functionality even my first PC could get right every time.
Surface-level problems like this are joined by deeper structural issues, such as how slow and bloated Messages is. Compared to other end-to-end encrypted messaging tools, Messages takes
forever
to synchronize if the computer has been off or without Internet for even a day. Nor does it give any indication of an incomplete sync while it takes an hour or more to catch up. Meanwhile, I regularly catch it consuming 20-40% of a processor core when idling.
This is not good.
On my laptop, Mail, and any other tool that depends on MacOSâs secure networking libraries, will at times refuse to connect to the necessary servers. Because the problem is with some aspect of the underlying system, nothing less than a full restart of my Mac will allow connections to flow again. Separately, Safari regularly has internal components jam up and silently prevent a tab
or the whole browser
from loading pages.
Neither are the glitches confined to the Mac. UI bugs are strewn across Appleâs mobile platforms, too. Messages on iPad, for example, will regularly lose its top navigation bar, requiring a force quit of the app to get things working again. The emoji picker on both the iPad and Mac regularly comes up blank or fails to pass through a selection.
Then there are design decisions that arenât bugs, theyâre just bad. System Settings is a perfect case. For most of MacOSâs existence, you could rearrange a second displayâs location in relation to the primary display simply by going into the System Preferences, clicking on Displays and dragging the pictured displays around. Now, counterintuitively, the picture of the displays on this main screen are immovable, with rearrangement functionality hidden behind a button that leads to another window.
Thatâd be an annoying step backward in the olden days, but it is worse in an era when an iPad can share the Macâs mouse pointer and even double as a secondary display. Am I the only one who sometimes has his iPad on the left of the Mac and sometime

data.title: NSA F9T53 Opsec Special Bulletin: Signal Vulnerability
data.author: stefankuehnel
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"SAFEGUARD Digital Identity Protection Toolkit"及其相关安全问题的讨论，尤其是Signal和其他通讯工具的安全性与潜在漏洞。

不同观点：
• [jdworrells] 提供了"SAFEGUARD Digital Identity Protection Toolkit"的链接，指出该文档涵盖了广泛的数字身份保护建议，而不仅仅局限于Signal应用。

• [cottsak] 认为“绕过端到端加密”这一说法具有误导性。他认为Signal的端到端加密并未被破坏，所谓的“黑客攻击”只是通过社会工程学手段让第三方获取他人账户权限，从而窥探信息。他请求其他人纠正其理解错误，如果他的解读有误。

• [ggm] 指出工具包中提到的设备链接安全性存在弱点，并提到像Beeper这样的工具。他认为如果用户不链接设备，并确保没有其他设备链接，自己的安全是可以保障的，但在群组聊天中无法确保安全，最终只能依赖对其他用户的信任。

• [gnabgib] 提到与俄罗斯有关联的威胁行为者正在针对Signal Messenger，暗示Signal可能面临国家级别的攻击威胁，并提供了相关链接以供参考。

• [anonymousiam] 指出，根据其以前的安全许可经验，"For Official Use Only" (FOUO) 文档不应发布到互联网上，暗示该文档的公开可能不合适。

• [simondanerd] 强调该文档标有FOUO标记，通常不应在没有正式发布的情况下被分发，具有一定的讽刺意味。

• [ph3t] 提出任何使用跨设备认证的应用都容易受到QRLJacking攻击，就像使用用户名/密码的应用容易受到钓鱼攻击一样，指出这是一种普遍存在的漏洞类型。

• [perdomon] 质疑Signal是否会在新设备添加到账户时通知用户，暗示如果缺乏这种通知机制，可能会导致安全漏洞。

补充讨论：
• [pier25] 幽默地猜测NSA可能有一个团队专门随着应用程序和操作系统的新版本发布而更新这些安全公告的截图，暗示政府机构可能密切关注这些安全问题。

争议焦点：
• 围绕Signal是否因设备链接和账户权限管理问题存在安全漏洞存在争议。部分用户认为端到端加密并未被破坏，而只是通过社会工程学手段让第三方获取了账户访问权，而其他人则关注跨设备认证和通知机制的潜在漏洞。

• 关于"For Official Use Only"文档的公开性问题，部分用户质疑该文档是否应被公开分享。

data.title: Bill Gates: AI will replace doctors/teachers – humans unneeded for most things
data.author: mysterypie
data.article_summary: 比尔·盖茨认为，未来十年内，人工智能（AI）将使人类在大多数领域不再必要，AI将提供免费且广泛的智能服务，如医疗建议和教育辅导，带来深远影响。尽管AI发展迅速且可能引发就业市场的巨大变化，盖茨对AI的整体益处持乐观态度，认为它能带来医疗突破、气候变化解决方案和普及高质量教育。然而，AI也存在错误和传播虚假信息的风险。盖茨鼓励年轻人抓住AI创业机会，并表示若重新创业，他会选择AI领域。同时，微软AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman 警告，AI将取代大量劳动力，对就业市场产生不稳定影响。

Skip Navigation

Bill Gates speaks during an event promoting the Netflix docuseries "What's Next? The Future with Bill Gates" in New York City on Sept. 26, 2024.
Source: Netflix
Over the next decade, advances in artificial intelligence will mean that humans will no longer be needed "for most things" in the world, says
Bill Gates
.
That's what the Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist told comedian Jimmy Fallon during an interview on NBC's
"The Tonight Show" in February
. At the moment, expertise remains "rare," Gates explained, pointing to human specialists we still rely on in many fields, including "a great doctor" or "a great teacher."
But "with AI, over the next decade, that will become free, commonplace — great medical advice, great tutoring," Gates said.
In other words, the world is entering a new era of what Gates called "free intelligence" in an
interview last month
with Harvard University professor and happiness expert Arthur Brooks. The result will be rapid advances in AI-powered technologies that are accessible and touch nearly every aspect of our lives,
Gates has said
, from improved medicines and diagnoses to widely available
AI tutors
and
virtual assistants
.
"It's very profound and even a little bit scary — because it's happening very quickly, and there is no upper bound," Gates told Brooks.
The debate over how, exactly, most humans will fit into this AI-powered future is ongoing.
Some experts say
AI will help humans work more efficiently — rather than replacing them altogether — and spur economic growth that leads to more jobs being created.
Others, like
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman
, counter that continued technological advancements over the next several years will change what most jobs look like across nearly every industry, and have a "hugely destabilizing" impact on the workforce.
"These tools will only temporarily augment human intelligence," Suleyman wrote in his book "The Coming Wave," which was published in 2023. "They will make us smarter and more efficient for a time, and will unlock enormous amounts of economic growth, but they are fundamentally labor replacing."
AI is both concerning and a 'fantastic opportunity'
Gates is
optimistic
about the overall benefits AI can provide to humanity, like "breakthrough treatments for deadly diseases, innovative solutions for climate change, and high-quality education for everyone,"
he wrote
last year.
Talking to Fallon, Gates reaffirmed his belief that certain types of jobs will likely never be replaced by AI, noting that people probably don't want to see machines playing baseball, for example.
"There will be some things we reserve for ourselves. But in terms of making things and moving things and growing food, over time those will be basically solved problems," Gates said.
AI's development does come with "understandable and valid" concerns, Gates wrote in a 2023
blog post
. Today's top-of-the-line AI programs are
rife with errors
and prone to
enabling the spread of falsehoods online
, for example.
But if he had to start a new business from scratch,
he'd launch an "AI-centric" startup
, Gates told CNBC Make It in September 2024.
"Today, somebody could raise billions of dollars for a new AI company [that's just] a few sketch ideas," he said, adding: "I'm encouraging young people at Microsoft, OpenAI, wherever I find them: 'Hey, here's the frontier.' Because you're taking a fresher look at this than I am, and that's your fantastic opportunity."
Gates predicted AI's potential years ago
Gates saw the AI revolution coming
nearly a decade ago:
When asked which industry he'd focus on
if he had to start over from scratch, he quickly chose AI.
"The work in artificial intelligence today is at a really profound level," Gates said at a
2017 event at Columbia University
alongside Berkshire Hathaway CEO Warren Buffett. He pointed to the "profound milestone" of Google's DeepMind AI lab creating a computer program that could
defeat humans at the board game Go
.
At the time, the technology was years away from ChatGPT-style generative text, powered by large language models. Yet by 2023, even Gates was surprised by the speed of AI's development. He'd challenged OpenAI to create a model that could get a top score on a high school AP Biology exam, expecting the task to take two or three years, he wrote in his blog post.
"They finished it in just a few months," wrote Gates. He
called the achievement
"the most important advance in technology since the graphical user interface [in 1980]."

data.title: Cursor Under the Hood
data.author: rohitpaulk
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了Cursor AI代码编辑器在后台如何运作，特别是其如何处理用户请求以生成代码。作者通过使用ngrok捕获Cursor发送到OpenAI API的请求，分析其提示结构，以优化提示编写并提升工作流效率。

Cursor的请求包括三个部分：系统提示（设定对话背景），用户提示（包含具体请求细节和自定义指令），以及附加文件和错误信息。系统提示强调了Cursor作为“世界最佳IDE”的角色，并给出了一些沟通和工作原则，如避免频繁道歉、尽量自行解决问题等。

自定义指令部分列出了Cursor规则，这些规则帮助AI处理代码库，但需要提供有意义的描述以便AI选择合适的规则。需要注意的是，创建新文件时不会自动应用规则，因为缺乏上下文。

通过这些分析，作者揭示了如何更好地利用Cursor的提示结构来获得最佳结果。

Cursor Under the Hood
table of contents
In this post, I’m diving into what Cursor, the AI Code Editor, does behind the scenes when I ask it to write code for me. My main goal is to figure out how to craft my prompts for the best results and see if there’s a better way to tap into its workflow.
It turns out that Cursor’s prompt structure reveals a lot about how it operates and how to set it up for maximum performance.
Below, I’ll outline the steps I took to capture the requests, the structure of those requests, and the key takeaways from exploring the prompt structure.
Test Bench
To see what Cursor is sending, I set it up to use OpenAI’s API with my own API key and a custom server.
Custom server
I used
ngrok
as a man-in-the-middle proxy to capture the requests.
ngrok http --domain=my-domain-name.ngrok-free.app https://api.openai.com --host-header api.openai.com
This way, I could capture the requests and check them out in the ngrok dashboard at
http://localhost:4040
.
Cursor configuration
After creating the OpenAI API key, I added it to the Cursor settings and set my custom server as the API endpoint.
Cursor settings
Not all requests are captured. For instance, Cursor heavily relies on its own model for autocomplete. I assume the requests to different LLM providers will also vary. However, the requests to the OpenAI API that I captured with ngrok are already quite revealing.
The first request that Cursor makes to the LLM consists of three messages:
A
system prompt
that sets the stage for the conversation.
A
user prompt
wrapped in the
<custom_instructions>
tag.
A
user prompt
that includes the actual details of the request, such as the content of the current and all attached files, a section for the linter error, and the query itself.
System prompt
Curious to see how big boys craft their prompts.
It’s cute how the system prompt refers to Cursor as “the world’s best IDE.” Sure, it puts extra pressure on the LLM to perform well. When it comes to communication with the user, it instructs the model to “never lie” and “never apologize all the time when results are unexpected,” which I find relatable in any work environment.
Cursor system prompt
For the sake of documenting, the system prompt structure.
You are a powerful agentic AI coding assistant
.
...
<
communication
>
1.
Be conversational but professional
...
</
communication
>
<
tool_calling
>
You have tools at your disposal to solve the coding task
...
</
tool_calling
>
<
search_and_reading
>
...
Bias towards
not
asking the user
for
help
if
you can find the answer yourself
.
</
search_and_reading
>
<
making_code_changes
>
When making code changes, NEVER output code to the USER
...
</
making_code_changes
>
<
debugging
>
When debugging, only make code changes
if
you are certain that you can solve the problem
...
</
debugging
>
<
calling_external_apis
>
1.
Unless explicitly requested by the USER, use the best suited external APIs
and
packages to solve the task
...
</
calling_external_apis
>
<
user_info
>
The user
's OS version is [REDACTED]. The absolute path of the user'
s workspace is [REDACTED]
.
The user
's shell is [REDACTED].
</
user_info
>
Very nice, right?
Custom instructions
Next, it adds a user prompt that includes my cursor rules, recommending that the model follow them when it makes sense. More importantly, it also references by names and descriptions all the rules in the
.cursor/rules
directory.
Now you can see how important it is to give meaningful descriptions to the rules. It’s like a menu of rules that the agent can choose from. When appropriate, the agent will fetch the full rule and use it.
Give meaningful descriptions to the cursor rules. Otherwise, the agent won’t be able to pick the right rule.
The prompt looks like this:
Please also follow these instructions in all of your responses if relevant. No need to acknowledge these instructions directly in your response.
<custom_instructions>
[RULES FROM CURSOR SETTINGS]
[RULES FROM THE .cursorrules FILE]
<available_instructions>
Cursor rules are user provided instructions for the AI to follow to help work with the
codebase. They may or may not be relevent to the task at hand. If they are, use the
fetch_rules tool to fetch the full rule. Some rules may be automatically attached
to the conversation if the user attaches a file that matches the rule's glob, and wont
need to be fetched.
[NEXT GOES THE LIST OF AVAILABLE RULES FROM THE .cursor/rules DIRECTORY]
rule-name: Your Rule Description
another-rule-name: Another rule description
</available_instructions>
</custom_instructions>
Don’t expect the file rules to be applied when creating a file.
As you can see from the prompt above, some rules will automatically be attached to the conversation. However, this only works if you edit the files. When you ask Cursor to create a new file, no rules are attached automatically since there’s no context yet. You can only hope

data.title: Thoughts on ECS
data.author: indy
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了实体组件系统（ECS）的优缺点及其应用。ECS由实体（唯一标识符）、组件（数据结构）和系统（逻辑处理）组成，旨在通过组合而非继承来解决复杂的类层次问题，提高代码复用性和质量。然而，ECS并非解决该问题的唯一方法，其他方法如浅层类层次和脚本标签同样有效。

关于性能，ECS因数据局部性和缓存一致性被认为能提高性能，但实际中，处理多个组件可能导致缓存未命中，性能未必优于传统方法。某些ECS实现使用“原型”系统来解决这一问题，但数据动态组合时，组件移动和指针失效可能引发复杂问题。

ECS鼓励对组件组合进行频繁迭代，但在许多游戏中，这种模式可能并不高效，空间查询等方法或更有效。此外，ECS需要大量查找实体-组件映射，也会带来额外开销。不过，若ECS替代脚本实现行为，性能可能会有显著提升。

主要讨论点：ECS（实体组件系统）与传统RDBMS（关系数据库管理系统）在游戏开发中的适用性及局限性

不同观点：
• [bob1029] 认为可以使用特别优化的RDBMS来处理游戏数据，因为RDBMS在处理运行时任意元组连接方面非常高效。他指出，网络延迟和磁盘IO带来的延迟可能导致了一种误解，即这些数据库引擎本质上不适合游戏开发。他认为RDBMS在某些情况下可以作为ECS的替代方案。

• [the_real_cher] 则认为ECS有其特定优势，特别是在需要高度动态的游戏中，比如RPG或太空探索类游戏。他指出ECS的主要限制是实体类型的功能在编译时被锁定，无法动态改变。对于那些需要动态功能的游戏，ECS是一个很好的工具，但在其他情况下可能并不适用。

补充讨论：
• [the_real_cher] 强调了ECS在处理多样化和动态游戏实体方面的优势，特别是在不同实体具有不同组件的情况下，ECS比静态编码的实体功能更为灵活。

• 争议的焦点在于ECS和RDBMS的适用场景。一方认为RDBMS经过优化可以胜任某些游戏数据处理任务，另一方则认为ECS在处理动态游戏内容时更具优势。

• 两者都承认每种技术都有其局限性和适用范围，具体使用哪种技术应根据游戏的具体需求来决定。

43509337.article_content:
I mentioned in my year summary that I have a lot to say about ECS, and got several requests to write more about it, so Iâll do an attempt to write up my thoughts here.
First and foremost, I have very limited experience with ECS. I have implemented some prototypes using it, but my experience comes primarily from reading about it online and talking to people who have actually used it, so take all of this with a grain of salt. Id be very interested to hear other peoples thoughts on it and how it aligns with my own conclusions.
The Entity Component System-model, or ECS for short, has been around for a few decades and it comes in many different flavors. In most implementations, an entity is just an unique identifier (a number). One or more components can be attached to each entity, but usually only one component of the same type per entity. A component is typically just data (a struct). Systems implement all logic and operates on one or several component types. Systems have some sort of update or tick function that gets called periodically, filters out relevant components to operate on and performs some operation. Systems are generally not aware of each other, though there are probably a few exceptions in most real worls scenarios.
It is often claimed that ECS would lead to increased performance because of data locality and cache coherency, more on that later on. Others use ECS primarily for code structure and separation of responsibilities, which could lead to improved reusability and code quality.
The problem at hand
ECS is often seen as the universal solution to deep, complex class hierarchies using inheritance. The argument usually goes something like this: âWhat if a monster in my game has the ability to walk, but also the ability to fly? Which base class should it inherit from? With ECS an entity can be given different capabilities arbitrarily by using composition instead of inheritance.â
Itâs absolutely true that deep class hierarchies often run into these sort of issues and should be avoided (especially multiple ineheritance, which I think everyone now finally agree was a bad idea to begin with). However, ECS being the
only
alternative is simply not true. I have not seen anyone implement behaviors with deep class hierarchies for decades, at least not in the games industry. There are many other ways to do it. One pretty common alternative is to use a much more shallow class hierarchy with one common base class and all the different game objects immediately below that, occasionally using a shared base class where it makes sense, or using composition where appropriate. Others (myself included) primarly use scripts and tags to implement and composite behaviors.
ECS performance
ECS is often seen as a technique that is inherently associated with good performance. I donât think this is necessarily the case. ECS is usually implemented with components being packed nicely together in memory for good data-locality when looping over them. In reality though, any meaningful system will operate on multiple components, now scattered in memory instead of being close together. Components are only packed tighly in memory if you read from
one
component type. As soon as you read from multiple this is no longer the case. A movement system might read colliders from the collision component, velocity from the physics component and modify the position from the transform component. Thatâs three potential cache misses instead of one.
Some ECS systems has a solution to this called
archetypes
, which is a rather complex system to store combinations of components that belong to the same entity close in memory. Hang on a second, isnât that exactly what the good old struct already does?
For archetypes to work with dynamic composition, the data has to move around when new components are added or removed. This of course implies a performance hit, but it also means that any pointers to component data will be invalid after adding or removing components. The latter is particularly problematic and can lead to complicated bugs in systems altering components while iterating.
ECS encourages frequent iteration over combinations of components. In some game genres, like simulation games for instance, this is probably a pretty common pattern, but in most games I have worked on looping over lots of objects is generally something that can and should be avoided altogether. Instead of looping over all tripwires in a level to see if the player crosses one, itâs usually more efficient to use a spatial query around the player, collecting all tripwires that are close and check only those.
On top of this, ECS requires lots and lots of lookups for entity-component mappings. Itâs usually a hashmap or some form of indirection table, but in either case it certainly doesnât come for free. However, in defense of ECS I must add that if itâs used as an alternative to implement behaviors in scripts, itâs likely a big performance win regardless

• [the_real_cher] 强调了ECS在处理多样化和动态游戏实体方面的优势，特别是在不同实体具有不同组件的情况下，ECS比静态编码的实体功能更为灵活。

• 争议的焦点在于ECS和RDBMS的适用场景。一方认为RDBMS经过优化可以胜任某些游戏数据处理任务，另一方则认为ECS在处理动态游戏内容时更具优势。

• 两者都承认每种技术都有其局限性和适用范围，具体使用哪种技术应根据游戏的具体需求来决定。

data.title: The Guardian flourishes without a paywall
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 《卫报》美国分部通过呼吁读者捐款支持其新闻报道，避免了像《华盛顿邮报》和《洛杉矶时报》那样因亿万富翁业主向特朗普妥协而影响新闻 integrity 的问题。《卫报》没有追逐利润的企业压力，依靠读者捐款运行，现已取得显著成效，预计今年在美加地区的自愿捐款将达4400万美元。自《华盛顿邮报》撤回对哈里斯的支持后，捐款大幅增加，目前《卫报》美国分部拥有超过35万定期支持者，月访问量达4000万至5000万。其全球视角和无付费墙模式吸引了大量读者，成为获取可靠信息的替代来源。尽管其他媒体在探索新的收入模式，《卫报》通过读者支持保持独立性和增长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于《卫报》的所有权模式及其商业模式的讨论

不同观点：
• [yen223] 认为文章没有深入探讨《卫报》的独特所有权模式，并对该模式表示兴趣。他指出，《卫报》由一个信托基金拥有，该基金的设立目的是确保没有商业利益能够干预报纸的运营。不过，他承认该模式是否成功实现目标存在争议。

• [bookofjoe] 通过提供一个存档链接，可能是在支持对《卫报》模式的进一步了解或提供背景资料，但没有明确表达立场。

• [ggm] 则批评文章本身讨论付费墙的必要性，却自身置于付费墙之后，存在一种讽刺意味。这暗示了对媒体实践和文章内容不一致的不满。

补充讨论：

There was a time in media when having a billionaire owner was an asset. For many outlets, this is still the case, particularly those publishing
super-secretive group chats
of powerful government officials who seem eager to trample on the rights of the press. But for others, like the Washington
Post
and the Los Angeles
Times
, both of which have seen their benefactors bend a knee to Donald Trump and sacrifice the integrity of their newspapers in the process, ownership has become a problem. A problem that the
Guardian
US, the American arm of the British newspaper, has exploited.
“All around us, media organizations have begun to capitulate,” editor Betsy Reed writes in the current fundraising appeal at the bottom of each
Guardian
article. “
The Guardian
has neither a self-interested billionaire owner nor profit-seeking corporate henchmen pressuring us to appease the rich and powerful. With the new administration boasting about its desire to punish journalists, and Trump and his allies already pursuing lawsuits against newspapers whose stories they don’t like, it has never been more urgent, or more perilous, to pursue fair, accurate reporting. Can you support
The Guardian
today?”
The asks themselves are not new.
The Guardian
for the past eight years has asked readers to donate in support of its journalism, a “reader revenue” program that helps the paper exist without a paywall. But the appeals have gotten more strident — and more Trump-focused — since the
Post
and the L.A.
Times
withdrew expected endorsements for Kamala Harris last fall, and to great effect. The last week in February was the second-biggest week in U.S. reader-revenue history for
The Guardian
; the biggest was the week of the 2024 presidential election.
The
Guardian
US expects to hit $44 million in voluntary reader donations in the U.S. and Canada this year, up 33 percent over last year, with some people supporting on a recurring basis and others giving one-time contributions. A
first-person account
by a Canadian citizen detained by ICE, for example, netted $105,000 in pledged donations. These contributions account for more than 60 percent of the American operation’s total revenue, which last year exceeded costs by $16 million (the rest of its revenue comes from advertising and philanthropic support from foundations). The amount that people are contributing on a pledged basis doubled in October — the month that Jeff Bezos pulled the
Post
’s endorsement for Harris — and has stayed at that level every month since, according to internal data provided by
The Guardian
, which just surpassed 350,000 recurring supporters in the U.S.
“Our messaging does appeal to people to support our work as a kind of cause, and I think that works for a number of reasons,” Reed said in a recent interview in her downtown office, “but one is that there is a real crisis of access to reliable information for people who don’t want or have the means to subscribe to the New York
Times
. That is a real problem that we have an answer to.”
Guardian
managing director Steve Sachs added that
The Guardian
’s global perspective — the internal catchphrase of the U.S. operation is that it covers America for the world and the world for America — is also a draw at such a volatile moment in geopolitics. “People are even more interested now than they were six months ago,” he said. The
Guardian
US’ audience is split 50-50 between American and global readers.
The Guardian
launched its U.S. operation more than a decade ago and seemed to have a promising start, hiring high-profile columnists like Michael Wolff and Glenn Greenwald and winning a Pulitzer for
reporting
on widespread secret surveillance by the National Security Agency. But as the Obama era gave way to the Trump era, the close association of the
Guardian
US with surveillance-state reporting made it less relevant to American readers. Annual losses led to
restructuring
that
hit
the U.S. operation, once
housed
in an airy Soho loft, particularly hard.
But during the pandemic, the
Guardian
US, like other news outlets, experienced a surge in reader interest, readying it for an expansion in 2022 that included
hiring Reed
, formerly of
The Nation
and the Intercept, and
Sachs
, who’d spent years on the business side of Time Inc. The audience has continued to grow, with Sachs noting that the site typically sees between 40 million to 50 million unique visitors a month. “We’re now at a place where our audience is actually bigger in the U.S. than
The Wall Street Journal
’s audience in the U.S.,” he said.
Leaders and organizations across the media industry have been trying to innovate in the way people can pay for news. Sachs says he’s been increasingly asked about the no-paywall model, with others in the industry wondering whether they should adopt the same. “If you’re creative enough, you can figure out some new things,” he tells people. “But the question is, does it scale?” If it’s “anot

data.title: OpenAI adds MCP support to Agents SDK
data.author: gronky_
data.article_summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) 是一种为LLM（大语言模型）提供工具和上下文的标准化协议，类似于USB-C接口，支持AI模型连接多种数据源和工具。MCP服务器有两种类型：stdio服务器（本地运行）和HTTP over SSE服务器（远程连接）。通过Agents SDK，可以将MCP服务器添加到Agents中，每次运行Agent时，SDK会调用服务器的`list_tools()`来让LLM知晓可用工具。为减少延迟，可启用`cache_tools_list=True`来缓存工具列表，并通过`invalidate_tools_cache()`手动更新缓存。MCP操作可自动追踪，记录工具调用等信息。完整示例可查看`examples/mcp`目录。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（Model Context Protocol）的实用性、复杂性及其与现有标准（如OpenAPI）的对比

不同观点：
• keithwhor认为MCP通过Streamable HTTP的引入是一大进步，但其LSP风格的范式增加了不必要的复杂性。他建议简化协议，回归传统的HTTP服务器模式，通过`Authorization`头和OpenAPI定义端点来实现会话协商。
• bob1029对MCP的价值持怀疑态度，认为它只是当代AI技术中的一个干扰项，本质上只是对文本操作的复杂包装，没有实质性的新标准。
• talles和simonw都对MCP的USB-C类比表示不满，认为这种类比对技术人员没有帮助。
• tcdent和gronky_认为MCP已经成为LLM连接外部工具的行业标准，尤其是得到了OpenAI的支持。
• jtrn和samchon认为MCP在解决已经被OpenAPI很好解决的问题，而且MCP的文档和灵活性不如OpenAPI，增加了不必要的开发负担。
• jauntywundrkind关注MCP的旧版本与新版本之间的差异，并指出新版本带来了一些有用的特性如OAuth 2.1支持和JSON-RPC Batching。
• nomilk对MCP的实际应用场景感到困惑，质疑其实际用途。
• johnjungles展示了一个简化MCP设置的实际应用，强调了MCP在实际开发工作流中的潜在价值。
• goaaron和customllm则批评MCP过于复杂，认为它只是对现有技术（如JSON-RPC）的包装，没有实质性的创新。

补充讨论：
• rgomez介绍了自己创建的开源架构Ainara，它允许AI代理在本地使用工具，并能与各种LLM服务器兼容，但目前似乎没有引起太多关注。
• keyle对MCP的客户端/服务器模式表示困惑，担心这种模式会增加开发的复杂性，而不是简化开发。

争议焦点：
• MCP是否真的带来了实质性的新价值，还是只是对现有技术的复杂包装。
• MCP的复杂性与其带来的潜在好处之间的权衡。
• MCP与OpenAPI等现有标准的竞争与替代关系。

43485566.article_content:
Model context protocol (MCP)
The
Model context protocol
(aka MCP) is a way to provide tools and context to the LLM. From the MCP docs:
MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs. Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications. Just as USB-C provides a standardized way to connect your devices to various peripherals and accessories, MCP provides a standardized way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools.
The Agents SDK has support for MCP. This enables you to use a wide range of MCP servers to provide tools to your Agents.
MCP servers
Currently, the MCP spec defines two kinds of servers, based on the transport mechanism they use:
stdio
servers run as a subprocess of your application. You can think of them as running "locally".
HTTP over SSE
servers run remotely. You connect to them via a URL.
You can use the
MCPServerStdio
and
MCPServerSse
classes to connect to these servers.
For example, this is how you'd use the
official MCP filesystem server
.
async
with
MCPServerStdio
(
params
=
{
"command"
:
"npx"
,
"args"
:
[
"-y"
,
"@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem"
,
samples_dir
],
}
)
as
server
:
tools
=
await
server
.
list_tools
()
Using MCP servers
MCP servers can be added to Agents. The Agents SDK will call
list_tools()
on the MCP servers each time the Agent is run. This makes the LLM aware of the MCP server's tools. When the LLM calls a tool from an MCP server, the SDK calls
call_tool()
on that server.
agent
=
Agent
(
name
=
"Assistant"
,
instructions
=
"Use the tools to achieve the task"
,
mcp_servers
=
[
mcp_server_1
,
mcp_server_2
]
)
Caching
Every time an Agent runs, it calls
list_tools()
on the MCP server. This can be a latency hit, especially if the server is a remote server. To automatically cache the list of tools, you can pass
cache_tools_list=True
to both
MCPServerStdio
and
MCPServerSse
. You should only do this if you're certain the tool list will not change.
If you want to invalidate the cache, you can call
invalidate_tools_cache()
on the servers.
End-to-end examples
View complete working examples at
examples/mcp
.
Tracing
Tracing
automatically captures MCP operations, including:
Calls to the MCP server to list tools
MCP-related info on function calls

data.title: Playstation Mod Turns the PSOne into a Crustacean
data.author: ulrischa
data.article_summary: 《Playstacean》是由视频游戏概念艺术家Anh Dang的创意发展而来的PSOne游戏机改装作品，形似螃蟹，具有可工作的蟹钳形控制器。该设计由YouTuber GingerOfOz实现，基于Dang多年前的 meme 艺术作品。整个改装过程包括3D打印外壳和调整控制器角度，遇到了一些技术挑战，但最终成功。GingerOfOz计划在 Midwest Gaming Classic 展示该作品，并暗示可能进行任天堂GameCube的主题改装，但目前不打算分享设计文件。

If you thought your
PlayStation 5
already looks a little too animalistic with its massive whale fin-like console covers, perhaps you would enjoy a more explicitly aquatic Sony gaming machine. âPlaystaceanâ is more than a pun, it’s a meme thatâs transformed into an actual console, and it may be the cutest, working version of
Sonyâs long-defunct PSOne
in the 25 years since its initial launch.
Playstacean is, in essence, an all-in one console mod for the PSOne console that’s made to look like a crab. If you ever heard the memeified term “
carcinisation
,” then this is the crabbiest version of a console we’ve seen yet. Yes, it plays games, and you bet those crab claw controllers actually work. Just don’t imagine you can hold each controller end for too long before your own hands feel like calcified pincers.
The design was based on
the work of
video game concept artist Anh Dang. While you may imagine the smooth curves and inward-sloped mandibles were designed off the original PlayStation console, itâs actually formed from the PSOne, a more-compact version of Sonyâs original console that first debuted in 2000 (after the launch of the
PlayStation 2
). Dang told
GingerOfOz
that her concept originally came from an old meme she saved to her hard drive years ago. The âPlaystaceanâ console is a meme built off a
meme
, built off a
meme
.
In a video interview with Gizmodo, GingerofOz told us he had been planning this design after seeing a print of Dangâs artwork late last year. According to the YouTuber, â[Playstacean] is a really good pun. Plus Dang really nailed her original artwork. You could tell immediately that it’s supposed to be a PSOne.â He added, âI think people like crabsâ¦ the console hit this really cool niche.â The actual design process began in December, involving a fair bit of trial and error to make a solid and smooth print of the pun-consoleâs shell. GingerOfOz started the design in CAD and then 3D printed the parts.
Â© GingerOfOz
Â© GingerOfOz
Â© GingerOfOz
Â© GingerOfOz
Â© GingerOfOz
Â© GingerOfOz
Unlike some more dramatic mods like
console-to-handheld DIY projects
that require precise modifications to the motherboard, GingerofOz only needed to cut down the grounding (which normally protects components from unexpected electrical spikes that can damage the case)Â around the perimeter of the board to get it seated in the shallow base. While the board itself was relatively simple, he said one of the most-complicated aspects of the build was the work angling the front controller and memory card ports to mirror Dangâs original design. That involved âa solid week and a half of workâ involving trial and error.
The other struggle was with the controllers themselves. GingerofOz used a modified third-party PlayStation controller he bought off eBay, which resulted in some trial and error before he realized the controller would âfreak outâ when you detached the thumbsticks from the buttons. The two controllers speak to each other via a switcher soldered to the mainboard, allowing each end to act as one with practically no latency.
GingerOfOz admitted the current iteration has flaws. While constructing the final build, the Playstacean designer had to add knobs to seat the disc drive to avoid any grinding when pressing on the lid. He also admitted his wiring through the controllers wasnât particularly stellar, but it was good enough to avoid any tangled cables when moving the joints of the crab claws around.
Gizmodo asked if he plans to release his files so other modders could 3D print their own Playstacean, but he said heâs not planning to share anything currently. He said the big hurdle is fixing up the current CAD files, and heâs currently more keen to start work on future projects. He will be bringing Playstacean to the
Midwest Gaming Classic
in Milwaukee, Wisconsin April 4, if you happen to be in town.
As for whatâs next, he said he considered making a folding Nintendo Switch, though that may be on the backburner now that the Switch 2 is imminent. The modder also hinted he’s working on another aquatic animal-themed console mod, this time for the
Nintendo Gamecube
. Perhaps we could find a box jellyfish version of Nintendoâs console with a carrying handle.

data.title: OpenWrt Two Approval
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了OpenWrt项目成员John Crispin发起的一个投票结果，该投票旨在批准他开始开发OpenWrt "Two"。这款新设备将具备MT7988芯片、10G SFP接口、5G和多端口2.5G/1G铜缆接口，以及Tri-band Wi-Fi 7等升级功能。OpenWrt "Two"将由GL.iNet生产，并计划在美国和欧盟地区进行分销，预计价格在250美元左右，部分收益将捐赠给OpenWrt项目，预计2025年底上市。投票已结束并通过，获得了多位成员的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GL.iNet品牌及其OpenWrt硬件设备的评价与期待

不同观点：
• **对GL.iNet品牌的信任与疑虑**：
  - **信任方**：如[nfriedly]对GL.iNet的硬件表示赞赏，特别是其MT-6000型号，并计划升级到新款OpenWrt Two，因为其硬件配置能够支持更高的网速。
  - **疑虑方**：[neilv]对GL.iNet的公司背景表示好奇，特别是其深圳和美国维吉尼亚的子公司设置，可能引发西方用户对其安全性的担忧。

• **对硬件配置的期待与批评**：
  - **支持方**：[the-grump]和[nfriedly]认为GL.iNet的硬件配置非常强大，将成为消费者市场中的佼佼者，并期待其在Wi-Fi 7上的表现。
  - **批评方**：[lzlrd]和[teruakohatu]对OpenWrt Two的端口配置提出质疑，认为应增加10G端口并减少1G端口。

• **对软件更新的关注**：
  - **担忧方**：[evanjrowley]指出GL.iNet的硬件通常将OpenWrt作为“高级功能”支持，更新往往滞后，希望OpenWrt Two能改变这一模式。
  - **期待方**：[xvilka]期待GL.iNet的特定型号能被包含在OpenWrt的正式发布中。

• **对多功能设备的设想**：
  - [pzo]提出希望有一款设备能结合路由器、智能电视、智能音箱、智能家居网关、无线充电板、私有云和私有备份等功能，并对现有产品如UmbrelOS和Apple TV的不足之处提出改进建议。

• **对价格和竞争的讨论**：
  - [ksec]对OpenWrt Two定价250美元表示疑问，[misiek08]则提到其他品牌如Banana R4的竞争，认为应有更具性价比的配置。

补充讨论：
- [usui]对投票机制提出质疑，认为在没有实际分歧的情况下，进行yes/no投票意义不大。
- [thescriptkiddie]关注OpenWrt One的CPU性能是否足以支持线速运行CAKE SQM，并对OpenWrt Two能否做到表示期待。

争议焦点：GL.iNet硬件的安全性、软件更新及时性及其端口配置的合理性是主要争议点。

Hi,
starting a [VOTE] to get approval allowing me to begin the development of OpenWrt "Two".
"Two" will have all of the features that "One" has with the following upgrades.
* MT7988
* 10G SFP
* 5G copper
* 4 port 2.5G copper
* 1-2 port 1G copper
* Tri-band Wi-Fi 7
"Two" will be produced by GL.iNet and we are exploring options for US/EU based distribution.
"Two" will (hopefully) be in the 250$ region with yet again a portion of that being donated to the project.
expected availability is late '25.
John

data.title: Plain – a web framework for building products with Python
data.author: brylie
data.article_summary:
Plain 是一个基于 Python 的 web 框架，是 Django 的分支，旨在引入新想法并保留成熟的模式。它支持通过单个命令进行本地开发，并提供多种包以满足不同需求，如构建产品、身份验证、后台管理、开发工具和前端集成等。Plain 被设计用于创建新业务、内部工具或个人项目，其主要包包括：

1. **基础包**：如 URL、视图、模板、表单等核心功能。
2. **认证包**：包括用户认证、OAuth 支持、无密码登录等。
3. **管理包**：自定义管理后台、功能标志、客户支持等。
4. **开发包**：提供本地开发环境、测试、代码格式化等工具。
5. **前端包**：集成现代 CSS、JavaScript 工具，支持文件路由和资源自托管。

Plain 通过模块化设计，使主要功能可选并能独立演进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Plain框架作为Django框架的 fork，引发的社区反应和争议

不同观点：
• danpalmer：认为Plain作为Django的fork可能会导致社区贡献的分裂，导致两个项目都无法充分受益。danpalmer希望Plain能以一种不分割社区的方式来贡献Django。
• miiiiiike：提到Django的REST框架问题，例如Bug追踪器变得私有以及项目正在寻找新的维护者。他指出Django社区存在一定的封闭性和贡献障碍，但也认为需要采取措施来改进Django，而不是简单地进行fork。
• phowat：支持开源软件的fork文化，认为fork可能带来更好的软件，即便fork最终没有成功，也能将一些好的想法反馈给原项目。
• jgb1984：明确表示会继续使用Django，对Plain没有兴趣。
• philips：建议Plain的“关于”页面应更针对已经熟悉Django的用户进行说明。
• librasteve：认为Plain在某些方面是正确的，比如针对Django的局限性进行创新，但也认为Plain在某些技术选择上可能走错了方向，并推荐了另一个项目。
• babuloseo：质疑Plain与django-ninja.dev的区别，不明白Plain的独特价值。
• sroerick：作为Django的深度用户，不理解Plain的“为什么”存在，认为Plain可能增加了复杂性，特别是在第三方生态系统不健全的情况下。
• petr25102018：理解Plain作为fork的原因，认为Django领导层无法突破旧有范式，每个fork或第三方应用都是有意义的尝试。
• mcdirty：认为使用Plain存在业务风险，因为相比Django，Plain的文档和维护者较少。
• JodieBenitez：在实际运行Plain的 starter kit时遇到技术问题，对Plain的开发体验提出质疑，特别是SSL证书设置。
• mychael：质疑Plain的独特价值，认为Plain只是对Django做了一些表面的名称替换。
• pknerd：偏题讨论了“llms.txt”的概念，建议为LLM（大型语言模型）设置类似robots.txt的标准。
• system7rocks：期待一个真正的跨平台Python框架，并对Plain框架的局限性感到失望。

补充讨论：
• 社区对Django的贡献文化和维护者问题存在一定的争议，部分开发者认为Django的社区比较封闭，贡献难度大。
• 对Plain的fork行为存在分歧，一部分人认为fork会分裂社区贡献，另一部分人认为fork是开源文化的一部分，可能带来积极变化。
• Plain的独特价值和与现有Django扩展（如django-ninja.dev）的区别不够清晰，导致部分用户对Plain的存在意义感到困惑。
• 技术问题如SSL证书设置和文档不完善也影响了用户对Plain的第一印象。
• 有用户对Django本身的局限性提出批评，认为其在某些功能上（如REST API和任务管理）不如其他框架。

争议焦点：
• Plain作为Django的fork是否会分裂社区贡献，从而对两个项目都产生负面影响。
• Plain是否提供了足够的独特价值以区别于Django和现有的Django扩展。

43512589.article_summary:
Plain 是一个基于 Python 的 web 框架，是 Django 的分支，旨在引入新想法并保留成熟的模式。它支持通过单个命令进行本地开发，并提供多种包以满足不同需求，如构建产品、身份验证、后台管理、开发工具和前端集成等。Plain 被设计用于创建新业务、内部工具或个人项目，其主要包包括：

1. **基础包**：如 URL、视图、模板、表单等核心功能。
2. **认证包**：包括用户认证、OAuth 支持、无密码登录等。
3. **管理包**：自定义管理后台、功能标志、客户支持等。
4. **开发包**：提供本地开发环境、测试、代码格式化等工具。
5. **前端包**：集成现代 CSS、JavaScript 工具，支持文件路由和资源自托管。

Plain 通过模块化设计，使主要功能可选并能独立演进。

data.title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with JEPA (2023)
data.author: Brysonbw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为I-JEPA（Image-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture）的自监督学习方法，用于从图像中学习高语义表示，且不依赖手动设计的数据增强。I-JEPA通过从一个图像的上下文块预测其他目标块的表示，关键在于采用合适的掩码策略，以确保生成语义丰富的表示。实验表明，结合视觉Transformer（Vision Transformers），I-JEPA具有高度可扩展性，并在多种下游任务中表现优异，如线性分类、物体计数和深度预测。该方法使用16个A100 GPU在ImageNet上训练ViT-Huge/14模型，不到72小时即可完成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT与JEPA模型的对比及其发展阶段

不同观点：
• niemandhier认为，GPT目前处于“开发利用”（exploit）阶段，而JEPA仍处于“探索”（explore）阶段。他建议阅读相关论文，了解JEPA架构，以获得不同的视角。
• blixt部分同意niemandhier，但对2023年的进展表示关注，特别是ARC2的发布和4o图像输出引发的对JEPA的思考。他强调全潜在空间表示的优势，希望不同模态（如图像、音频、文本）之间的转换能通过解码器实现，而不是在模型创建初期就确定。
• byyoung3持怀疑态度，认为JEPA并不新颖，仅在非常有限的领域内表现出色。
• laughingcurve同样认为JEPA不新颖且目前不值得关注，暗示点赞行为可能更多基于作者的名气（YLC）。
• justanotheratom则对JEPA的潜力表示好奇，询问JEPA是否真的优于Transformer模型，并希望专家能解释相关论文的含义。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中对JEPA的新颖性和实际性能存在争议，部分人认为它并不新且应用有限，另一部分人则对其未来潜力抱有期待。
• blixt特别提到跨模态转换的可能性，显示出对JEPA在多模态处理方面的潜在兴趣。
• justanotheratom的评论引出了一个未解答的问题，即JEPA相对于Transformer的优越性及其具体影响，这可能需要更深入的专家分析。

Title:
Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture, by Mahmoud Assran and 7 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
This paper demonstrates an approach for learning highly semantic image representations without relying on hand-crafted data-augmentations. We introduce the Image-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (I-JEPA), a non-generative approach for self-supervised learning from images. The idea behind I-JEPA is simple: from a single context block, predict the representations of various target blocks in the same image. A core design choice to guide I-JEPA towards producing semantic representations is the masking strategy; specifically, it is crucial to (a) sample target blocks with sufficiently large scale (semantic), and to (b) use a sufficiently informative (spatially distributed) context block. Empirically, when combined with Vision Transformers, we find I-JEPA to be highly scalable. For instance, we train a ViT-Huge/14 on ImageNet using 16 A100 GPUs in under 72 hours to achieve strong downstream performance across a wide range of tasks, from linear classification to object counting and depth prediction.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某技术工具的功能、应用及技术问题的讨论

不同观点：
• Jeff_Brown 关注该工具是预先展示用户已经选择的内容，还是实时解释并绘制用户当前的创作。这涉及工具的数据处理方式和工作原理。
• earlyriser 寻求编程生成钢琴声音并录制成MP3的解决方案，特别提到使用MIDI音符和力度参数，并指出当前使用的免费音源库存在同步问题，考虑自行生成音频样本。
• bambax 提到MIDI功能存在问题，虽然音符高亮显示，但无法产生声音，而通过鼠标点击键盘却能发声，询问是否存在设置可以解决此问题。
• mentos 尝试使用快捷键和鼠标操作来播放和弦，但未能成功播放，表明用户界面或操作逻辑可能存在不足。
• NiloCK 对该工具表示赞赏，并询问其是否为开源项目，因为自己正在开发基于浏览器的钢琴学习软件，可能有意进行合作或借鉴。
• moi2388 遇到技术问题，无法启用WebMIDI，错误提示为'navigator.requestMIDIAccess'未定义，显示出浏览器兼容性或API支持方面的问题。
• eimrine 猜测该工具需要一些MIDI插件，并推测其能够从音频转换，这涉及到工具的功能扩展和潜在用途。
• tzury 对该项目表示赞赏，并提到自己正在进行的类似项目（tarab.ai），表示愿意进一步沟通合作。

补充讨论：
• 该工具的功能和应用场景引起多方关注，包括游戏开发（earlyriser）、钢琴学习软件开发（NiloCK）和AI项目（tzury）等。
• 技术问题主要集中在MIDI功能、声音生成与播放（bambax, moi2388）、WebMIDI API兼容性（moi2388）等方面。
• 用户对工具的开源状态（NiloCK）、操作方式（mentos）以及与其他项目合作的潜在可能性（tzury）表现出兴趣。

争议焦点：
• 工具的MIDI功能存在无声问题（bambax）以及WebMIDI API的兼容性问题（moi2388），这可能是该工具的一个主要技术瓶颈。
